Theme Elements for Image Grobs

Source: R/theme-elements.R
element.Rd

In conjunction with the ggplot2::theme system, the following element_ functions enable images in non-data components of the plot, e.g. axis text.

  • element_futebol_badge(): draws Brazilian Soccer team badges instead of their abbreviations.

Usage

element_futebol_badge(
  alpha = 1L,
  colour = NA_character_,
  hjust = 0.5,
  vjust = 0.5,
  color = NULL,
  angle = 0,
  size = grid::unit(0.5, "cm")
)

Arguments

alpha

The alpha channel, i.e. transparency level, as a numerical value between 0 and 1. 1L skips alpha channel modification for more speed.

colour, color

The image will be colorized with this colour. Use the special character "b/w" to set it to black and white.

hjust

A numeric vector specifying horizontal justification. If specified, overrides the just setting.

vjust

A numeric vector specifying vertical justification. If specified, overrides the just setting.

angle

The angle of the element as a numerical value between 0° and 360°.

size

The output grob size as a grid::unit. If given a numeric, cm will be applied as unit.

Value

An S7 object of class element_futebol_badge.

Details

The elements translate Brazilian Soccer team abbreviations into badge images. Unknown abbreviations are drawn as a generic badge.

The complete themes of ggplot2 (e.g. ggplot2::theme_minimal()) set axis.text.x.bottom and axis.text.y.left directly. Elements set in axis.text.x or axis.text.y are then overwritten and no badge will be drawn. Please use the specific elements, i.e. axis.text.x.bottom, axis.text.x.top, axis.text.y.left or axis.text.y.right.

See also

geom_futebol_badges(), and ggpath::element_path() for more information on valid team abbreviations, and other parameters.

Examples

# \donttest{
library(futebolplotR)
library(ggplot2)

team_abbr <- valid_team_names()

df <- data.frame(
  random_value = runif(length(team_abbr), 0, 1),
  team = team_abbr
)

# use badges for x-axis
ggplot(df, aes(x = team, y = random_value)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = team, fill = team), width = 0.5) +
  scale_color_futebol(type = "secondary") +
  scale_fill_futebol(alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x.bottom = element_futebol_badge())


# use badges for y-axis
ggplot(df, aes(y = team, x = random_value)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = team, fill = team), width = 0.5) +
  scale_color_futebol(type = "secondary") +
  scale_fill_futebol(alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y.left = element_futebol_badge())


# black and white badges with transparency
ggplot(df, aes(x = team, y = random_value)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x.bottom = element_futebol_badge(colour = "b/w", alpha = 0.6))

# }
